permutationLabel: Strangulation (fever, tachycardia, peritonism, lactate, CT signs)
summary: 67-year-old man, previous laparotomy, pain now constant, T 38.4 °C, HR 118, localised peritonism, WBC 19.4, lactate 4.1; CT: closed loop with reduced wall enhancement.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Constant abdominal pain, distension and vomiting
inputs.hpi: Laparotomy for a stab wound 20 years ago. 20 hours of abdominal pain, colicky at first but constant and severe for the last 6 hours, now worst on the right. Vomiting, no flatus since yesterday. Feels hot and shaky. Known small bowel obstruction from adhesions treated conservatively 3 years ago.

exam.general: Unwell, sweaty, tachycardic. Temperature 38.4°C, pulse 118/min, BP 104/66, RR 22.
exam.abdomen: Distended. Localised peritonism in the right lower abdomen with guarding and rebound tenderness. Midline laparotomy scar. Hernial orifices clear. Quiet bowel sounds.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Closed-loop small bowel obstruction with whirl sign in the right lower quadrant. A 40 cm ileal segment shows reduced mural enhancement, mesenteric oedema and free fluid — features of strangulation.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Strangulated adhesive small bowel obstruction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Adhesive small bowel obstruction with strangulation: closed-loop obstruction with reduced bowel wall enhancement, fever, peritonism and lactate 4.1. Emergency laparotomy.

emergencyLevel.note: Strangulation signs (fever, tachycardia, peritonism, lactate, CT) mandate emergency surgery.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Constant abdominal pain, distension and vomiting' gives 'urgent'.

mustInclude.note: The Plan tab text is the documented plan; for strangulation it must contain the operation.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Same ordering fix; the strangulation variant's surgical phase then carries the operation into the documented plan.

mustExclude.note: Bologna: non-operative management and contrast challenge are contraindicated when strangulation/peritonitis is present; delay increases resection and mortality.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: Documented plan = 'Small Bowel Obstruction — Non-Operative Trial (Drip and Suck)' and the Gastrografin step, for CT-proven strangulation with lactate 4.1. | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): forbidden management item present in ios.radiation.plan: "water-soluble contrast study (gastrografin) at 24h - therapeutic + diagnostic"
mustExclude.proposedFix: Check sbo_strangulation before sbo_adhesional (specific-first) and drop the conservative phase whenever strangulation words, lactate > 2 with peritonism, or closed-loop appear.

guideline.name: WSES Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (2017 update)
guideline.section: CT with IV contrast for strangulation signs; non-operative management (NGT, fluids) up to 72 h without strangulation; water-soluble contrast challenge (colon within 24 h predicts success); surgery for strangulation, peritonitis or failed NOM; virgin abdomen and hernia causes
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines for sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening (do not use qSOFA alone), antibiotics within 1 h of shock, blood cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypoperfusion, vasopressors, source control
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: strangulation. Every sign the Bologna guideline lists is present; the documented plan must be emergency surgery, never the 72-hour non-operative trial. The assessment text uses the ordinary phrase 'adhesive small bowel obstruction with strangulation'.
